definitions.full: H5922. al עַל preposition upon, over, on account of, above, to, against (Biblical Hebrew and General Aramaic id. ); — suffix 1 singular עֲלַי ; 2 masculine singular עליך Kt (so Egyptian Aramaic, Cooke No. 77, A 5, 6, B 8 , S-C Pap. A 3, B 5 +), עֲלָךְ , Qr ( עֲלַךְ ᵑ7 , Dalm § 47, 2 ) Dan 3:12 6 t. Daniel; Ezra 7:18 ; 3 masculine singular עֲלוֺהִי (so Nabataean, Palmyrene; Egyptian Aramaic עלוי S-C A 6 +) Dan 3:28 +, עֲלֹהִי Ezra 6:11 ; 3 feminine singular עליה Kt (so Egyptian Aramaic, S-C D 24 ), עֲלַהּ Qr (so ᵑ7 ) Dan 4:14 ; 5:21 ; 1 plural עֲלֵינָא Ezra 4:12 , עֲלֵ֑ינָא 4:18 ; 5:17 Baer (Gi עֲלֶ֑ינָא ); 3 masculine plural עֲלֵיהֹם (so Nabataean, CIS ii. 226 ; Egyptian Aramaic, S-C Pap. F 5, 8 +) 7:24 , עֲלֵיהוֺן 5:1 , 3 ; — 1. a. upon , Dan 2:10 , 28 , 46 ; 5:5 , 7 ; 6:11 + often, 4:26 מַלְכוּתָא עַלהֵֿיכַל ( 2Sam 11:2 ); to be established מַלְכוּתִי עַל 2 Samuel 4:33 (compare 2Chr 1:1 ; Biblical Hebrew II. 1) to lay an impost upon , Ezra 7:24 ; to trust on , Dan 3:28 ; after a verb of motion, עַל מְטָא to come upon , 4:21 ; 4:25 ; of times, to pass over , 4:13 ; 4:20 ; 4:22 ; 4:29 ; Ezra 5:1 עֲלֵיהוֺן יִשְׂרָאֵל אֱלָהּ בְּשֻׁם i.e. (named) over them. b. idiomatic (as in Biblical Hebrew; see II. 1 d ) of the person who is the subject of an emotion or experience, Dan 5:9 עֲלוֺהִי שָׁנַיִן וְזִיוֺתִי were changed upon him, 7:28 ; 6:19 עֲלוֺהִי נַדַּת וְשִׁנְּתֵהּ (compare 2:1 ). c. on accusative of (Biblical Hebrew 1f b), Dan 3:16 עַלדְּֿנָה מִּתְגָּם . So in עַלדְּֿנָה on this accusative Ezra 4:15 , 22 ; 5:17 , עַלמָֿה wherefore ? Dan 2:15 ; and דִּי דִּבְרַת עַל (see ׳דְּ ). d. on behalf of ( ib. 1f c ), Ezra 6:17 . e. regarding, concerning ( ib. 1f g ), Dan 2:18 ; 5:14 , 29 ; 6:6 ; 6:13 ; Ezra 7:14 +? 2 over , with verbs of ruling, appointing, etc., Dan 2:48-49 , 3:12 ; 4:14 +, Ezra 4:20 ; 6:18 . 3 in a comparative sense, above, beyond , Dan 3:19 ; 6:4 . 4 expressing direction: a. to , of a person, after a verb of motion (compare Biblical Hebrew 7c a a), Dan 2:24 ; 4:31 ; 4:33 ; 6:7 ; 6:16 ; Ezra 4:12 , 23 + often; after to send (a letter, etc.) 4:11 , 17 , 18 ; 5:6 +, write 4:7 , prophesy 5:1 ; of the direction of the mind ( ib. 7c c ), Dan 3:12 ; 6:14 (twice in verse); 6:15 ; compare Ezra 5:5 אֱל ׳וְעֵין עַל הֲוַת (compare Jer 40:4 and אֶל Psa 34:16 ). b. against , Dan 3:19 , 29 ; 5:23 ; 6:5 ; 6:6 +; Ezra 4:8 ; 7:23 . 5 in such phrases as טְאֵב עַל, שְׁפַר (to be) good or acceptable to (as in Syriac and late Hebrew: see Biblical Hebrew 8 ), Ezra 5:17 טָב מַלְכָּא עַל אִם , 7:18 (twice in verse); Dan 4:24 ( יִשְׁמַּר ), 6:15 ( בְּאֵשׁ ), 6:24 ( טְאֵב ). — compare the synopsis of meanings in Lzb 340 .

Be it known to the king that the Jews who came up from you have come to us to Jerusalem. They are building the rebellious and bad city, and have finished the walls, and repaired the foundations.
Now because we eat the salt of the palace, and it is not appropriate for us to see the king’s dishonor, therefore we have sent and informed the king,

that search may be made in the book of the records of your fathers. You will see in the book of the records, and know that this city is a rebellious city, and hurtful to kings and provinces, and that they have started rebellions within it in the past. That is why this city was destroyed.
Then the king sent an answer to Rehum the chancellor, and to Shimshai the scribe, and to the rest of their companions who live in Samaria, and in the rest of the country beyond the River:
The letter which you sent to us has been plainly read before me.
I decreed, and search has been made, and it was found that this city has made insurrection against kings in the past, and that rebellion and revolts have been made in it.
There have also been mighty kings over Jerusalem, who have ruled over all the country beyond the River; and tribute, custom, and toll, was paid to them.
Be careful that you not be slack doing so. Why should damage grow to the hurt of the kings?
